title: Build your first LED circuit
safety: Only use a 5V USB supply or a 9V battery or lower.
Never connect an LED directly to the supply without a resistor.
Disconnect power before changing the wiring.

steps.title: Identify the parts
steps.goal: Learner identifies LED, resistor and breadboard and knows which LED leg is the anode.
steps.intro_spoken: Let's start. Put the LED, the resistor and the breadboard in front of you and take a photo.
steps.visual_success_criteria: An LED (two legs, one longer), a resistor (striped body) and a breadboard are visible.
hint_levels: Look for a part with two legs.
Compare the two LED legs. Which is longer?
The longer LED leg is the anode, the plus side.
steps.check_question: Which LED leg connects to plus?

steps.title: Why a resistor?
steps.goal: Learner explains that the resistor limits the current so the LED does not burn out.
steps.intro_display: Why does an LED need a resistor?
steps.intro_spoken: Before we build: think about what would happen if you connected the LED straight to the battery.
hint_levels: What flows through the LED when it lights?
Too much current makes parts hot. What stops that?
The resistor limits the current through the LED.
steps.check_question: What does the resistor do for the LED?

steps.title: Build the circuit
steps.goal: Learner builds supply plus -> resistor -> LED anode, LED cathode -> supply minus, all in series.
steps.intro_spoken: Now build the circuit on the breadboard. When you are done, take a photo.
steps.visual_success_criteria: Resistor and LED are in series in one current path; LED long leg faces the plus side; both supply wires are connected.
hint_levels: Think about current flowing in one loop.
Where should the resistor go in that loop?
Connect the resistor in series with the LED.
steps.check_question: Does your LED light up now?

steps.title: Find the bug
steps.goal: Learner finds a deliberately introduced fault (LED flipped) and explains why it breaks the circuit.
steps.intro_display: I changed something. Find the bug!
steps.intro_spoken: Ask your partner to flip the LED around. Then find out why it stopped working.
steps.visual_success_criteria: LED orientation is visible; after the fix the long leg faces the plus side again.
hint_levels: Which part only works in one direction?
Check the LED legs. Where is the long one?
The LED was reversed. Flip it back.
steps.check_question: Why did the LED stop working?

steps.title: Explain it back
steps.goal: Learner explains the whole circuit: current path, LED direction and resistor purpose.
steps.intro_spoken: Last step. In your own words: why does your circuit work?
hint_levels: Follow the current from plus to minus.
Mention the resistor and the LED direction.
Current flows through resistor and LED, anode to plus.
